transcript.text: hotpoint SA2 oven not heatin on fan, grill ok. wat does SA2 mean??

First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. “SA2” is a Hotpoint oven series/prefix, rather than an error code. It is not enough on its own to identify the exact version or parts. With the grill working but fan oven not heating, the most likely cause is the fan-oven rear heating element or its connections. The fan-oven selector switch, thermostat/control circuit are also possible. First rule out the simple settings: 1. Check the function knob is on the fan-oven heating symbol — normally a fan inside a circle — not defrost (fan only), light-only or an eco setting. Set 180°C and leave it 15 minutes. If it then heats, it was a setting issue.
2. Check the clock is showing the correct time and is in manual mode, not flashing or showing AUTO/timed cooking. Some ovens inhibit heating when left in automatic mode after a power interruption.
3. On the fan-oven setting, does the fan run but the cavity stay cold? That strongly points towards the rear fan-oven element, but a failed selector contact, thermostat/control or wiring can give the same symptom. Do not remove panels while it is connected to power. If the fan runs and it remains cold on the correct setting with the clock in manual, an engineer can test the element and its supply safely; that is usually the next sensible step.
yeah its on the fan setting and clock is in manual. the fan isnt actually spinning tho, just a low hum from the back. had a slight hot smell from the back once but not now

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use the oven again until it has been checked by a qualified oven engineer. A low hum from the rear with the cooking fan not turning points most strongly to a seized/jammed cavity fan motor or something preventing the fan blade turning. The grill working and the clock being in manual make a timer setting fault unlikely. The fan-oven element may also need testing, but the non-spinning fan is the first fault to deal with; a fan oven should not be run with its circulation fan stalled. With the cooker isolated and fully cool, an engineer should inspect the fan blade/motor, its wiring and connectors, then test the fan-oven element and selector supply.
